uncited: The method optimizes the parallel generation of MIP-map levels for a sparse voxel octree by preventing redundant thread execution.
It relies on a 2D node map derived from the light-view map to identify which threads are targeting the same 3D octree node.
*   **Input:** The sparse voxel octree structure, the light-view map (a 2D array of photon indices), and the target MIP-map level for the current pass.
**Node Lookup:** For each thread, determine the target octree node for the current MIP-map level.
*   **MIP Level:** The current level of the MIP-map being generated.
Typical values depend on the octree depth.
*   **Node Map Levels:** The number of levels in the node map pyramid corresponds to the number of MIP-map levels.
*   **Degenerate Input:** If the light-view map is empty, no threads are launched.
If the octree has no nodes at the target level, the lookup fails.
The complexity per thread remains similar, but the total work is reduced.
*   **When Not to Use:** When memory is constrained, or when the overhead of maintaining the node map outweighs the benefits of thread termination (e.g., very small octrees).
It is part of the voxel cone tracing technique for real-time global illumination.
